chunks: The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said to a man: “Did you begin the morning fasting?” He said: “No.” He said: “Then did you visit a sick person?” He said: “No.” He said: “Then did you follow a funeral?” He said: “No.” He said: “Then did you feed a poor person?” He said: “No.” He said: “Then return to your family and be with them, for indeed that is a charity from you to them.”

key_terms.أَهْلِكَ: your family; one’s household or spouse
key_terms.جَنَازَةً: a funeral; the funeral procession one accompanies
key_terms.صَائِمًا: fasting; observing sawm at the start of the day
key_terms.صَدَقَةٌ: charity; a rewarded act of giving or benefit
key_terms.مَرِيضًا: a sick person; someone visited as an act of compassion
key_terms.مِسْكِينًا: a poor person in need of food or support

ai.seo_question: How can being with one’s family be considered a charity in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith presents several virtuous acts, including fasting, visiting the sick, following a funeral, and feeding a poor person. When the man had done none of them, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم directed him toward his family, teaching that intimacy with one’s family can also be an act of charity. The narration highlights the broad scope of righteous deeds in Islam, including within family life.
